title: Understanding VASP Power Profiles on NVIDIA A100 GPUs
problem: Understanding how VASP power consumption varies with different workloads and parallelism configurations on GPU-accelerated supercomputers, and determining the feasibility of applying power-aware scheduling strategies in HPC environments.
motivation: Power efficiency is critical for exascale supercomputing systems to operate within limited power budgets.
method: Empirical characterization study of VASP power behavior on the Perlmutter A100 GPU system at NERSC. The authors vary VASP inputs, parallelism parameters, and apply power capping to GPUs to measure power consumption changes and resulting performance impact.
key_novelty: Demonstrates that VASP power usage varies significantly more with workload type than with parallel concurrency, and that 50% TDP power capping achieves less than 10% performance loss for most workloads.
contributions: Comprehensive power profile characterization of VASP on NVIDIA A100 GPUs
Evidence that workload characteristics are more influential than parallelism on power behavior
Demonstration that aggressive power capping (50% TDP) can be applied with minimal performance degradation
Assessment of power-aware scheduling feasibility for HPC applications

metrics.other: less than 10% performance loss at 50% TDP power capping

primary_theme: GPU power profiling and power-aware HPC scheduling
